requirement:
The harness MUST record the source text it supplies to the model, including
mandatory inputs and additional reads, using the existing evidence input formats
defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.ci.rust_item_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs`, and
{cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs`. The harness MUST create these records
itself so ordinary evidence validation can check them later.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is met.** The harness records the source text it supplies to the model, and it builds those records itself.

**Implementation**
- **Building the records.** Every input comes from `InputSelector::resolve` / `to_input` in `src/inputs.rs` (about lines 85–145). That is the same resolver CI uses. It emits file-range inputs (`file`, `line_start`, `line_end`, `text`), Rust-item inputs, requirements inputs (`requirements`, `matches`, `text`) and definition inputs (`definition`, `text`). Ordinary evidence validation can therefore re-check them under `requirements.ci.inputs`, `requirements.ci.rust_item_inputs`, `requirements.ci.requirements_inputs` and `requirements.definitions.inputs`. The model never supplies input records. `assess` builds the evidence object itself, with `"inputs": sources.recorded_inputs()`, and the model supplies only the determination and rationale.
- **Mandatory inputs.** `AssessmentSources::prepare` and `prepare_function` build `mandatory` through `source_input`. This covers the subject, cited and referenced requirements, existing evidence selectors, and the required terminology from `definition_inputs`. In `assess`, `pending` starts as these mandatory inputs.
- **Additional reads.** `tools::read` (habeas) and `tools::search` (ripgrep) each return a `ToolDelivery` holding the input records plus the required terminology definitions. `assess` pushes these into `pending`. A file-range read with no `line_end` records the actual EOF line. `list_files` returns no inputs, so directory listings are not recorded.
- **When they are recorded.** `assess` calls `sources.record_inputs(&pending)` only after a provider response succeeds, then clears `pending`. This covers the mandatory inputs, and the tool deliveries that were sent in the next request, including the request that ends in `submit_judgment`. `record_inputs` deduplicates. A failed tool call adds nothing to `pending`. A throttled attempt leaves `pending` unchanged and `continue`s, so inputs are recorded only once the request that carries them succeeds, as `provider_backoff` requires.

**Tests**
- `function_judgments_use_boolean_schema_and_harness_owned_inputs` (`src/authoring/mod.rs`) checks that `record["inputs"] == sources.mandatory_inputs()` for function attestations.
- `reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms` (`src/authoring/tools.rs`) covers these points:
  - `list_files` yields no inputs.
  - A Rust-item read yields the item plus its term definition.
  - Nothing is recorded until `record_inputs` is called.
  - Recording twice deduplicates.
  - A file read with no `line_end` records the actual EOF line.
  - Malformed, mixed and unknown request forms are rejected.
- `ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free` (`tests/authoring_cli.rs`) covers these points:
  - Mandatory definition inputs and the ripgrep file-range windows (lines 1–11 and 10–12) end up in the saved evidence.
  - Repeated deliveries are deduplicated.
  - Failed reads (`absent.txt`) and directory listings are not recorded.
- `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_…` checks that requirements, definition and Rust-file inputs appear in the evidence.
- `bedrock_cli_…` checks that a delivered range is recorded.
- `throttled_requests_retry_unchanged_and_record_every_attempt` checks that after eight 429 retries the final record's `inputs` equal the mandatory inputs, so inputs are recorded once and only on success.

**Gaps.** I found no explicit FIXMEs. One thing I did not see is a test that feeds the recorded inputs back through the CI validator. The inputs come from the same resolver the validator uses, so I consider this minor.

text: The harness MUST record the source text it supplies to the model, including
mandatory inputs and additional reads, using the existing evidence input formats
{cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs`. The harness MUST create these records
itself so ordinary evidence validation can check them later.

For a file-range input, Habeas MUST verify that `line_start` and `line_end` identify an inclusive, ordered range in `file` and that `text` exactly matches the current raw lines in that range. Habeas MUST report missing files, invalid ranges, and changed lines.

For a Rust-item input, Habeas MUST parse `rust_file` with `syn` and resolve `rust_item` to exactly one item. It MUST determine an inclusive range of complete raw source lines containing that item, including attached doc comments, attributes, and leading citation comments. It MUST compare `text` with those lines without serializing the `syn` tree, and derive the range again during validation for display and reference coverage. Moving unchanged lines because of edits earlier in the file MUST NOT invalidate the input. Habeas MUST report a missing file, parse failure, invalid or ambiguous selector, or changed lines.

For a requirements input, Habeas MUST match the glob in `requirements` against all defined requirements and named examples. It MUST recompute the matches during validation, sort their full names, and compare them with `matches`. It MUST take each match's complete raw fenced declaration, including its opening and closing lines, concatenate those declarations in full-name order with one blank line between them, and compare the resulting raw lines with `text`. It MUST retain every match's current source file and inclusive line range for display and reference coverage. A glob matching no definitions MUST be invalid. Adding, removing, renaming, or changing a matched definition MUST invalidate the stored input; moving an unchanged declaration within the book MUST NOT. Errors MUST identify the glob and affected definitions when available.

Evidence inputs MAY have a definition form containing exactly `definition` and `text`. `definition` MUST identify one named definition; `text` MUST contain its complete raw fenced declaration as source lines, including its phrase option and explanatory body.

Validation MUST reject missing definitions and changed snapshot text, identifying the definition and showing a compact diff when available. Moving an unchanged definition within its chapter MUST NOT invalidate its snapshot. Evidence displays MUST show the definition name, current source location, and recorded text.

request, retaining its prompt, history, tools, and pending inputs. It MUST NOT
restart the assessment or repeat already completed tool calls. A permanent
input/context-length error, authentication failure, or invalid request MUST
remain an error; mentioning tokens in an error message alone MUST NOT trigger
The backoff window MUST start at one second and double after each consecutive
throttled attempt, up to sixty seconds. Each delay MUST be randomly selected
between half and all of that window to spread parallel retries. An available
provider `Retry-After` value, in seconds or HTTP-date form, MUST be honored as a
minimum delay even when longer than the window. A successful response MUST reset
backoff for the next completion request. There MUST be no retry-attempt limit;
interruption MUST cancel both the wait and further retries.
Each attempt MUST be recorded under {cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_requests`.
Hidden SDK retries MUST remain disabled so the harness can account for attempts.
Transient retries MUST NOT be reported as finished judgments or terminal
assessment errors while recovery is still in progress. Pending inputs MUST be
recorded as evidence only after the request succeeds.
